name: Hadar
overview: Hadar was a male king of the Edomites, succeeding Baal-hanan as ruler. He is noted in Scripture as the king who reigned from the city of Pau. His identity is firmly rooted in the Edomite tribal context as recorded in Genesis 36:39.
namesAndTitles: The primary name recorded is Hadar, without a specific meaning provided. An alternate form, Hadad, means 'thunderer' in Hebrew, though this is noted separately in 1 Chronicles 1:50 and may reflect a variant or related name. No divine naming is indicated for Hadar.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture infers that Hadar was married to Mehetabel, as noted in Genesis 36:39. Beyond this relationship, no additional family connections are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Hadar's significance lies in his role as a king of Edom, marking the continuation of Edomite leadership after Baal-hanan. His reign from Pau highlights the established governance structure among the descendants of Esau. This lineage of kings provides insight into the political organization of Edom as presented in the biblical genealogies.
